findings.title: Cache deletion does not refresh the cache status shown in the UI
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the parent onSuccess, and the parent is onChanged. Nothing invalidates `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation, which does invalidate it in onSettled. The `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in the dropdown therefore stays at the old timestamp after the cache is deleted, until some unrelated refetch happens. The PR test plan explicitly requires that the UI updates after deletion.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or cache status repository method
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler performs an authorization check (credential must belong to the user) and a destructive deleteMany, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds uses a groupBy with _max. Neither is covered by any test in the PR. The authorization path in particular should have a test that a user cannot delete another user's credential cache.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data on every cache refresh, bumping updatedAt for all calendars
findings.body: CalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache (line 1024 of the service diff) calls updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) on every cache population. Because SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is @updatedAt, this rewrites updatedAt on every selected calendar under the credential, including event-type-scoped ones, on each refresh. The PR notes say this value is not displayed in the frontend, so the write is unused load and a misleading timestamp. The method also has no guard against an empty update, and the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt change is only justified in the notes, not in code.

findings.title: Comment says CalendarCache has no updatedAt, which this PR now adds
findings.body: The TODO above the findFirst orderBy says updatedAt 'doesn't exist yet' in the CalendarCache table. This PR adds that column, so the comment is now wrong and misleads future readers about whether updatedAt can be used for ordering.

findings.title: Timestamp is hardcoded to en-US instead of the user's locale
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) even though the rest of the component is localized via useLocale. Users with other locales see an English date format next to translated labels. The locale from useLocale should be used.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and breaks on Linux
findings.body: The script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with `sed -i '' -E ...`. The empty argument after -i is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux, many CI/dev containers) the empty string is treated as the script and the command fails, so the .env file is not updated. The script is not portable and nothing in the PR documents that it is macOS-only.

findings.title: deleteCache does not check the credential's app type before deleting cache rows
findings.body: The handler only verifies that the credential belongs to the user, then deletes all calendarCache rows with that credentialId. It does not check that the credential is a calendar credential, and the UI only offers the action for Google Calendar. A direct tRPC call can clear cache rows for any owned credential. This is low impact but inconsistent with the UI's restriction.

findings.title: Cache deletion stays available when connection modification is disabled, and the Alert branch now gates on it
findings.body: The previous code hid the remove button whenever disableConnectionModification was set. The new dropdown still shows the 'Delete cached data' action in that case, because canDisconnect is separate from hasCache. Meanwhile the error Alert branch (line 124) now also passes disableConnectionModification, which it did not check before. The intended permission model for these two actions is not stated or tested.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, which is unrelated to this feature and not declared as a dependency
findings.body: This change replaces ts-node with `npx tsx` for dev:cron, but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies. npx will fetch it at runtime, which can be slow or fail offline. The change is unrelated to calendar cache management and should be split into its own PR.
